cards.text: Again the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, the prophet. God calls him son of man and starts with a look back. When the people of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their own ways and deeds.

cards.question: God poured out His wrath on the people of Israel. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The blood they shed and their idols
The battles they lost to their enemies
The temple tax they refused to pay

cards.question: After pouring out His wrath, God scattered the people of Israel among the nations.

cards.text: And wherever they go, they profane God's holy name. It comes down to what people say when they see them.

cards.question: Wherever Israel goes among the nations, what do people say about them?

answers.text: They are the LORD's people yet had to leave His land
They are the people who defeated Egypt and Edom
They are a people without any god of their own

cards.text: But God had concern for His holy name, the one Israel profaned everywhere they went. So He gives Ezekiel a message for the house of Israel.

cards.question: In His message to the house of Israel, God says He will act for their sake.

cards.text: Not for their sake. For His holy name. Friend, I relate, because NOBODY pulled me out of that junk drawer for looking sharp. My edges were GONE.

cards.question: God says He'll show the holiness of His great name. When He does, what will the nations know?

answers.text: That Israel is the greatest nation
That their own idols have power

cards.question: God says He will show His holiness in ___ before the eyes of the nations.

cards.text: Now the turn, friend. God says He'll gather them out of all the countries and bring them back into their own land.

cards.question: God says He'll sprinkle something on the people of Israel so they'll be clean. What is it?
God says He will cleanse Israel from all their impurities and all their idols.

cards.text: Then comes the big one. God says He'll give them a new heart and put a new spirit within them.

cards.question: God says He'll remove one kind of heart from Israel and give them another. Which swap is it?

answers.text: A heart of stone for a heart of flesh
A heart of iron for a heart of gold
A heart of fear for a heart of courage

cards.text: A heart of stone. Friend, I once pressed into dough straight out of the fridge and bent my whole handle, and my mustache STILL won't talk about it.

cards.question: God says He will put His ___ within Israel and cause them to walk in His statutes.

cards.text: With that, they'll carefully observe His ordinances. And they'll live in the land God gave their forefathers.

cards.question: Back in the land, God says Israel will be His people and He will be their God.

cards.text: God says He'll save them from all their uncleanness and won't bring famine on them. He'll call for the grain and make it PLENTIFUL.

cards.question: God makes the fruit and crops plentiful so Israel will no longer bear ___ among the nations because of famine.

cards.text: Then, God says, Israel will remember. Their evil ways and their wicked deeds.

cards.question: When Israel remembers their evil ways, how does God say they'll feel about themselves?

answers.text: They will loathe themselves for their iniquities
They will boast that it is all behind them
They will blame the nations around them

cards.text: Then God says that line again: "It is not for your sake that I will act". When the oven timer goes off twice, friend, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Right after saying it's not for their sake, God tells Israel to be proud of how far they've come.
God names the day He'll resettle Israel's cities and rebuild the ruins. Which day is it?

answers.text: The day He cleanses them from all their iniquities
The day the nations bring them gifts of gold
The day a new king takes the throne in Jerusalem

cards.text: The desolate land gets worked again. No more lying there desolate for everyone passing through to see.

cards.question: People will say the land that was desolate has become like the garden of ___.

cards.text: And the cities once ruined, desolate and destroyed? Fortified and inhabited, and friend, I went from the back of a junk drawer to my own PLANET, so I am NOT surprised.

cards.question: The nations that remain around Israel will know that Israel rebuilt the ruins by its own strength.

cards.text: God says it plain: "I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it." Then one more promise: once again He'll hear the plea of the house of Israel.

cards.question: God says He'll multiply Israel's people. He compares them to something seen in Jerusalem at the appointed feasts. What is it?

cards.text: The ruined cities fill with flocks of people, and God says, "Then they will know that I am the LORD." Stone hearts swapped and ruins rebuilt, so friend, a worn-out stamper like me never stood a chance.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Not for their sake. For His holy name.' That only restates the answer to card 7 and what card 6 already said about God's concern for His holy name. The rest is the joke, so the card adds nothing new from the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question says God sprinkles something 'so they'll be clean,' and the right answer is 'Clean water.' The repeated word 'clean' makes the right answer stand out from 'Holy oil' and 'Fine ashes.'

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'A heart of stone.' only repeats the answer to card 5. The rest of the card is the cold-dough joke, so it tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Spirit' is capitalized, while the wrong answers 'angel' and 'prophet' are lowercase. The capital letter marks the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer 'reproach' sounds like Bible language, while the wrong answers 'debt' and 'taxes' sound modern. A baker can pick the right answer by its tone alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'A worn-out stamper like me never stood a chance' usually means someone was doomed or beaten. That is the opposite of the intended point that God's renewing power would surely reach him too, so the punchline doesn't land. 'Stone hearts swapped' also reaches back to verse 26 on a card that cites only verse 38.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
